newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean listed firms' H1 sales seen up 8.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean listed firms' H1 sales seen up 8.1 pct.

text.p: Sales of South Korea's listed companies were expected to rise 8.1 percent in the first half of this year from a year earlier, Dongsuh Securities said on Thursday.

In a forecast of first-half business results of 553 enterprises which fiscal years end in December, the brokerage house said half-year sales growth slowed sharply from an 18.7 percent rise a year before.
"Sluggish business in the sectors of vehicles, semiconductors and textiles was to blame for the slowdown," said a Dongsuh satement.
In the report, companies now under supervision were excluded, the statement said.
The report also showed recurring profits of the listed firms were estimated to rise 0.8 percent in the first half, compared with a fall of 36.9 percent a year ago.
Ordinary profits, usually before-tax, are total revenues minus total costs which are incurred in normal business activities.
Sales of manufacturing companies rose 7.7 percent in the six-month period, against a 13.8 percent rise a year before. Their recurring profits fell 21.5 percent, against a fall of 48.4 percent.
